claim: Ikaros-ERt2 fusion proteins are retained in the cytoplasm of pre-B cells until their release by the ERt2 ligand 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT).
source: Ikaros-ERt2 fusion proteins are retained in the cytoplasm of pre-B cells (Ferreirós-Vidal et al., 2013) until their release by the ERt2 ligand 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT), which initiates the translocation of Ikaros-ERt2 within minutes (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The statement cites a previous publication (Ferreirós-Vidal et al., 2013) and references figures showing the translocation process.

claim: 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT) initiates the translocation of Ikaros-ERt2 within minutes.
source: Ikaros-ERt2 fusion proteins are retained in the cytoplasm of pre-B cells (Ferreirós-Vidal et al., 2013) until their release by the ERt2 ligand 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT), which initiates the translocation of Ikaros-ERt2 within minutes (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Association with DAPI-dense pericentromeric gamma-satellite regions suggests that Ikaros binds DNA immediately after nuclear translocation.
source: Association with DAPI-dense pericentromeric gamma-satellite regions containing Ikaros binding sites (Brown et al., 1999, 1997; Hahm et al., 1998) suggests that Ikaros binds DNA immediately after nuclear translocation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from observed association with pericentromeric regions and citations to previous work identifying Ikaros binding sites.

claim: Ikaros binds sequence motifs of gamma satellites, the core repeat unit of mouse pericentromeric heterochromatin.
source: Ikaros binds sequence motifs of gamma satellites, the core repeat unit of mouse pericentromeric heterochromatin (Brown et al., 1999, 1997; Cobb et al., 2000; Hahm et al., 1998; Klug et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: ChIP-PCR showed a steep rise in Ikaros binding to Igll1 promoter within 5 min.
source: ChIP and quantitative PCR showed a steep rise in Ikaros binding to Igll1 promoter within 5 min (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The Igll1 promoter has two Ikaros sites, Ik1 at −83nt and Ik2 at −107nt from the Igll1 TSS.
source: The Igll1 promoter has two Ikaros sites, Ik1 at −83nt and Ik2 at −107nt from the Igll1 TSS.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the genomic structure of the Igll1 promoter.

claim: An EBF motif is embedded in the Ik1 site.
source: An EBF motif is embedded in the Ik1 site, and gel mobility shift experiments demonstrate mutually exclusive binding of EBF1 and Ikaros (Thompson et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Gel mobility shift experiments demonstrate mutually exclusive binding of EBF1 and Ikaros at the Igll1 promoter.
source: An EBF motif is embedded in the Ik1 site, and gel mobility shift experiments demonstrate mutually exclusive binding of EBF1 and Ikaros (Thompson et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The embedded EBF1 site is critical for Igll1 promoter activity.
source: Despite the presence of two additional EBF1 motifs at −198 and −228nt, the embedded EBF1 site is critical for Igll1 promoter activity (Mårtensson and Mårtensson, 1997) (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The rise in Ikaros binding 5 min after 4-OHT was not accompanied by a corresponding fall in EBF1 binding.
source: It was therefore surprising that the rise in Ikaros binding 5 min after 4-OHT was not accompanied by a corresponding fall in EBF1 binding (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental ChIP data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Increased Ikaros binding without simultaneous eviction of EBF1 5 min after 4-OHT suggests that Ikaros does not directly displace EBF1.
source: Increased Ikaros binding without simultaneous eviction of EBF1 5 min after 4-OHT suggests that Ikaros does not directly displace EBF1.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation that Ikaros binding increases without corresponding EBF1 decrease.

claim: Interactions of transcription factors with target DNA are often transient, and not all target sites for DNA binding factors are occupied at any given time.
source: Interactions of transcription factors with target DNA are often transient, and not all target sites for DNA binding factors are occupied at any given time (Elf et al., 2007; McNally et al., 2000; Poorey et al., 2013; Voss and Hager, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: EBF1 ChIP measured a gradual reduction in EBF1 binding between 15 and 60 min after 4-OHT.
source: Consistent with this prediction, EBF1 ChIP measured a gradual reduction in EBF1 binding between 15 and 60 min after 4-OHT (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental ChIP data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The abundance of nuclear Ikaros rises gradually over time.
source: The abundance of nuclear Ikaros rises gradually over time (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), yet ChIP shows that Ikaros binding flattens out after 5 min and shows little or no further increase after 15 min, even though declining EBF1 binding should release potential binding sites (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: ChIP shows that Ikaros binding flattens out after 5 min and shows little or no further increase after 15 min.
source: The abundance of nuclear Ikaros rises gradually over time (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), yet ChIP shows that Ikaros binding flattens out after 5 min and shows little or no further increase after 15 min, even though declining EBF1 binding should release potential binding sites (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The nuclear translocation of Ikaros abolished RNAP2 binding to promoters and gene bodies of the target genes Igll1 and Vpreb1.
source: ChIP sequencing (ChIP-seq) showed that the nuclear translocation of Ikaros abolished RNAP2 binding to promoters and gene bodies of the target genes Igll1 and Vpreb1 (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) that are repressed by Ikaros (Ferreirós-Vidal et al., 2013; Thompson et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and citations to previous work.

claim: RNAP2 occupancy remained unchanged at the nearby Top3b promoter, which is not regulated by Ikaros.
source: RNAP2 occupancy remained unchanged at the nearby Top3b promoter, which is not regulated by Ikaros (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Prior to nuclear translocation of Ikaros the Igll1 promoter showed a nucleosome-free region that was occupied by RNAP2.
source: Prior to nuclear translocation of Ikaros the Igll1 promoter showed a nucleosome-free region that was occupied by RNAP2.
evidence: The claim is based on MNase-seq data described in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Upon nuclear translocation of Ikaros the Igll1 promoter region became occluded by nucleosomes, and RNAP2 occupancy was reduced.
source: Upon nuclear translocation of Ikaros this region became occluded by nucleosomes, and RNAP2 occupancy was reduced (Figure 2A, inset and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by MNase-seq and ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: ChIP-PCR demonstrated a rapid decrease in RNAP2 occupancy at the promoters, gene bodies and transcription termination sites (TTS) of Ikaros-repressed genes.
source: ChIP-PCR demonstrated a rapid decrease in RNAP2 occupancy at the promoters, gene bodies and transcription termination sites (TTS) of Ikaros-repressed genes (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: RNAP2 occupancy decreased at promoters, gene bodies, and the 3' end of transcription units, suggesting that Ikaros represses Igll1 and Myc transcription by interfering with RNAP2 recruitment rather than elongation.
source: RNAP2 occupancy decreased at promoters, gene bodies, and the 3' end of transcription units (Figure 2B), suggesting that Ikaros represses Igll1 and Myc transcription by interfering with RNAP2 recruitment rather than elongation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the pattern of RNAP2 reduction shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Genome-wide, RNAP2 occupancy was significantly reduced at 372 downregulated genes 6 hr after Ikaros translocation.
source: Genome-wide, RNAP2 occupancy was significantly reduced at 372 downregulated genes 6 hr after Ikaros translocation (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by genome-wide ChIP-seq analysis presented in Table 1.

claim: The great majority of repressed genes with reduced RNAP2 occupancy showed a global reduction in RNAP2 binding to both the promoter and the gene body (324 of 372 or 87%).
source: The great majority of repressed genes with reduced RNAP2 occupancy showed a global reduction in RNAP2 binding to both the promoter and the gene body (324 of 372 or 87%).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of ChIP-seq data presented in Table 1.

claim: Only a small minority of repressed genes showed a block in RNAP2 elongation, as judged by preferential reduction of RNAP2 occupancy over the gene body (15 of 372 or 4% of genes with reduced RNAP2 occupancy).
source: Only a small minority of repressed genes showed a block in RNAP2 elongation, as judged by preferential reduction of RNAP2 occupancy over the gene body (15 of 372 or 4% of genes with reduced RNAP2 occupancy).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of ChIP-seq data presented in Table 1.

claim: Transcriptional repression of Ikaros target genes occurred by reduced RNAP2 recruitment, and a block in RNAP2 elongation was the exception.
source: Hence, transcriptional repression of Ikaros target genes occurred by reduced RNAP2 recruitment, and a block in RNAP2 elongation was the exception.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genome-wide analysis of RNAP2 occupancy patterns.

claim: Nucleosome occupancy increased with similar kinetics as RNAP2 eviction.
source: We assessed nucleosome occupancy of promoters and transcription start sites by PCR amplification of fragments protected from MNase digestion. Nucleosome occupancy increased with similar kinetics as RNAP2 eviction (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by MNase-PCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The abundance of Igll1 and Myc primary transcripts was reduced within minutes of Ikaros translocation with similar kinetics as RNAP2 eviction and increased nucleosome occupancy.
source: The abundance of Igll1 and Myc primary transcripts was reduced within minutes of Ikaros translocation with similar kinetics as RNAP2 eviction and increased nucleosome occupancy (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Triptolide triggers the global degradation of RNAP2.
source: Triptolide triggers the global degradation of RNAP2 (Manzo et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2011) and resulted in the near-complete loss of RNAP2 from whole cell lysates (Figure 3A, left) and from the Igll1 and Myc promoters (Figure 3B, left; the inactive Rex1 promoter is shown as a negative control).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work and experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Loss of RNAP2 reduced promoter occupancy by the basal transcription factor TFIIB.
source: Loss of RNAP2 reduced promoter occupancy by the basal transcription factor TFIIB (Figure 3B, center) but, interestingly, the Igll1 and Myc promoters remained sensitive to MNase in the absence of RNAP2 (Figure 3B, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The Igll1 and Myc promoters remained sensitive to MNase in the absence of RNAP2.
source: Loss of RNAP2 reduced promoter occupancy by the basal transcription factor TFIIB (Figure 3B, center) but, interestingly, the Igll1 and Myc promoters remained sensitive to MNase in the absence of RNAP2 (Figure 3B, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by MNase-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Accessibility of Ikaros target gene promoters is not simply a consequence of RNAP2 occupancy.
source: Hence, accessibility of Ikaros target gene promoters is not simply a consequence of RNAP2 occupancy.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that promoters remain accessible after RNAP2 depletion.

claim: Nuclear translocation of Ikaros-ERt2 efficiently reduced the accessibility of the Igll1 and Myc promoters even after RNAP2 depletion.
source: We next compared the impact of Ikaros on target gene promoters in control and RNAP2-depleted cells. Nuclear translocation of Ikaros-ERt2 efficiently reduced the accessibility of the Igll1 and Myc promoters even after RNAP2 depletion (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by MNase-PCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The demonstration that the Igll1 and Myc promoter regions remain accessible in the absence of RNAP2 mechanistically separates RNAP2 occupancy from promoter accessibility.
source: The demonstration that the Igll1 and Myc promoter regions remain accessible in the absence of RNAP2 mechanistically separates RNAP2 occupancy from promoter accessibility.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations regarding RNAP2 depletion and promoter accessibility.

claim: CHD4 depletion substantially reduced the impact of Ikaros on the accessibility of the Igll1 and Myc promoters.
source: We used RNA interference to deplete the NuRD-associated ATPase subunit Mi-2β/CHD4 encoded by Chd4 (Figure 4A). CHD4 depletion substantially reduced the impact of Ikaros on the accessibility of the Igll1 and Myc promoters (Figure 4B), indicating a key role for CHD4 in mediating Ikaros-induced nucleosome remodeling at the Igll1 and Myc promoters.
evidence: The claim is supported by MNase-PCR data shown in Figure 4B following CHD4 knockdown.

claim: CHD4 plays a key role in mediating Ikaros-induced nucleosome remodeling at the Igll1 and Myc promoters.
source: CHD4 depletion substantially reduced the impact of Ikaros on the accessibility of the Igll1 and Myc promoters (Figure 4B), indicating a key role for CHD4 in mediating Ikaros-induced nucleosome remodeling at the Igll1 and Myc promoters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CHD4 knockdown experiments.

claim: Ikaros-induced RNAP2 eviction and transcriptional repression were significantly delayed by Chd4-RNAi.
source: Ikaros-induced RNAP2 eviction and transcriptional repression were significantly delayed by Chd4-RNAi (Figure 4C), consistent with a role for CHD4-dependent chromatin remodeling in the silencing of Ikaros target genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-PCR and RT-PCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: ChIP-PCR showed a rapid increase in the binding of the NuRD subunits CHD4 and MBD3 to the Igll1 promoter after 4-OHT.
source: We next assessed the impact of Ikaros on the association of NuRD components with the Igll1 promoter. ChIP-PCR showed a rapid increase in the binding of the NuRD subunits CHD4 and MBD3 (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The onset of CHD4 and MBD3 recruitment mirrored increased Ikaros binding after 4-OHT.
source: The onset CHD4 and MBD3 recruitment mirrored increased Ikaros binding after 4-OHT (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of kinetic data from Figure 1B and Figure 4D.

claim: Increased binding of CHD4 and MBD3 was transient, returning close to their starting level by 6 hr.
source: In contrast to Ikaros, increased binding of CHD4 and MBD3 was transient, returning close to their starting level by 6 hr (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: CHD4 and the SWI-SNF-associated chromatin remodeler BRG1 can have antagonistic effects on transcriptional regulation.
source: CHD4 and the SWI-SNF-associated chromatin remodeler BRG1 can have antagonistic effects on transcriptional regulation (Curtis and Griffin, 2012; Gao et al., 2009; Ramirez-Carrozzi et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Genes activated by BRG1 were repressed by Ikaros (Odds ratio = 2.97, p=1.7×10−30).
source: Genes activated by BRG1 were repressed by Ikaros (Odds ratio = 2.97, p=1.7×10−30) and vice versa (Odds ratio = 3.32, p=9.5×10−31).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of gene expression data comparing Ikaros and BRG1 targets.

claim: Genes repressed by BRG1 were activated by Ikaros (Odds ratio = 3.32, p=9.5×10−31).
source: Genes activated by BRG1 were repressed by Ikaros (Odds ratio = 2.97, p=1.7×10−30) and vice versa (Odds ratio = 3.32, p=9.5×10−31).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of gene expression data comparing Ikaros and BRG1 targets.

claim: Ikaros-repressed genes were depleted among BRG1-repressed genes (Odds ratio = 0.62).
source: Conversely, Ikaros-repressed genes were depleted among BRG1-repressed genes (Odds ratio = 0.62) and vice versa (Odds ratio = 0.31; Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis presented in Table 2.

claim: Ikaros and BRG1 are broadly antagonistic in B cell progenitors.
source: This analysis indicates antagonistic regulation of target genes by Ikaros and BRG1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the overlap analysis of Ikaros and BRG1 target genes.

claim: At the peak of CHD4 and MBD3 binding, the Igll1 promoter showed a marked decline in BRG1 binding.
source: At the peak of CHD4 and MBD3 binding, the Igll1 promoter showed a marked decline in BRG1 binding (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: BRG1 association with the Igll1 promoter did not recover at later time points, when CHD4 and MBD3 binding returned to their starting levels.
source: BRG1 association with the Igll1 promoter did not recover at later time points, when CHD4 and MBD3 binding returned to their starting levels (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Broad inhibition of HDAC activity by trichostatin A (TSA) did not detectably interfere with Ikaros-induced loss of RNAP2, reduced promoter accessibility and early transcriptional repression of Igll1 and Myc.
source: Unexpectedly, broad inhibition of HDAC activity by trichostatin A (TSA) did not detectably interfere with Ikaros-induced loss of RNAP2, reduced promoter accessibility and early transcriptional repression of Igll1 and Myc (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Application of the HDAC1/2 inhibitor MS-275 confirmed that Ikaros initiated the transcriptional downregulation of Igll1 and Myc regardless of HDAC1/2 activity.
source: Application of the HDAC1/2 inhibitor MS-275 confirmed that Ikaros initiated the transcriptional downregulation of Igll1 and Myc regardless of HDAC1/2 activity (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: HDAC inhibition did not interfere with the transcriptional downregulation of Ikaros target genes in primary pre-B cells.
source: Similarly, HDAC inhibition did not interfere with the transcriptional downregulation of Ikaros target genes in primary pre-B cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data from primary pre-B cells shown in Figure 5C.

claim: TEV-induced nuclear translocation of Ikaros in the absence of ERt2 confirmed that HDAC activity was not required for the loss of accessibility or the transcriptional silencing of Igll1 and Myc.
source: To address the possibility that the ERt2 component of the Ikaros-ERt2 fusion protein might account for the apparent lack of HDAC activity in Ikaros-initiated gene silencing we performed experiments where the nuclear translocation of Ikaros was triggered by the inducible cleavage of Ikaros-TEV-ERt2 fusion proteins. TEV-induced nuclear translocation of Ikaros in the absence or ERt2 confirmed that HDAC activity was not required for the loss of accessibility (Figure 5D, left) or the transcriptional silencing of Igll1 and Myc (Figure 5D, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D using an alternative system.

claim: HDAC activity is dispensable for Ikaros-induced repression.
source: These data demonstrate that - unexpectedly - HDAC activity is dispensable for Ikaros-induced repression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments with HDAC inhibitors.

claim: Ikaros reduced the acetylation of histone H3 and H4 at the target genes Igll1 and Myc.
source: Consistent with this conclusion, ChIP experiments showed that although Ikaros reduced the acetylation of histone H3 and H4 at the target genes Igll1 and Myc, the kinetics of histone deacetylation were markedly slower than those observed for reduced promoter accessibility, RNAP2 eviction, and the decline in primary transcripts (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The kinetics of histone deacetylation were markedly slower than those observed for reduced promoter accessibility, RNAP2 eviction, and the decline in primary transcripts.
source: Consistent with this conclusion, ChIP experiments showed that although Ikaros reduced the acetylation of histone H3 and H4 at the target genes Igll1 and Myc, the kinetics of histone deacetylation were markedly slower than those observed for reduced promoter accessibility, RNAP2 eviction, and the decline in primary transcripts (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of kinetic data from ChIP experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Histone modifications are not likely drivers for early events in Ikaros-mediated repression.
source: Histone modifications are therefore not likely drivers for early events in Ikaros-mediated repression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that histone deacetylation occurs after transcriptional repression.

claim: Ikaros target gene transcription was not stably silenced 24 hr after Ikaros nuclear translocation in the presence of TSA.
source: While the immediate transcriptional downregulation of Ikaros target genes was unaffected by HDAC inhibition (Figure 5), we found that Ikaros target gene transcription was not stably silenced 24 hr after Ikaros nuclear translocation in the presence of TSA (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: TSA treatment for 24 hr did not affect Ikaros-induced nucleosome protection of short amplicons comprising 90–110 base pairs centred on peaks of MNase.
source: TSA treatment for 24 hr did not affect Ikaros-induced nucleosome protection of short amplicons comprising 90–110 base pairs centred on peaks of MNase (Figure 6B, bottom left).
evidence: The claim is supported by MNase-PCR data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: TSA reduced Ikaros-induced protection of longer amplicons of 130–140 bp, which represent the near complete length of 147 DNA base pairs associated with full nucleosomes.
source: In contrast, TSA reduced Ikaros-induced protection of longer amplicons of 130–140 bp, which represent the near complete length of 147 DNA base pairs associated with full nucleosomes (Figure 6B, bottom right).
evidence: The claim is supported by MNase-PCR data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In the absence of HDAC activity, nucleosomes at the Igll1 promoter and TSS may remain unstable or less evenly spaced.
source: These data suggest that in the absence of HDAC activity, nucleosomes at the Igll1 promoter and TSS may remain unstable (Henikoff et al., 2011) or less evenly spaced.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the MNase-PCR data with citation to previous work on nucleosome stability.

claim: At the Igll1 promoter and TSS, Ikaros triggered an increase in the occupancy not only of total histone H3, but also in the ratio of histone H2B over H3.
source: At the Igll1 promoter and TSS, Ikaros triggered an increase in the occupancy not only of total histone H3, but also in the ratio of histone H2B over H3 (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Prolonged HDAC inhibition significantly blunted the increase in the H2B/H3 ratio.
source: Prolonged HDAC inhibition significantly blunted this increase in the H2B/H3 ratio (Figure 6C), indicating that HDAC activity facilitated the assembly of H2B-containing nucleosomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: HDAC activity facilitated the assembly of H2B-containing nucleosomes.
source: Prolonged HDAC inhibition significantly blunted this increase in the H2B/H3 ratio (Figure 6C), indicating that HDAC activity facilitated the assembly of H2B-containing nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the H2B/H3 ratio data.

claim: In the absence of 4-OHT, only a small minority (8%) of Igll1 alleles were associated with γ-satellite DNA.
source: In the absence of 4-OHT, only a small minority (8%) of Igll1 alleles (green) were associated with γ-satellite DNA (red), the repeat unit of mouse pericentromeric heterochromatin (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D DNA-FISH data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Most (78%) Igll1 alleles were associated with γ-satellite DNA after 4-OHT.
source: In contrast, most (78%) Igll1 alleles were associated with γ-satellite DNA after 4-OHT (Figure 6D), indicating that increased nuclear Ikaros cells was sufficient for the repositioning of Igll1 to pericentromeric heterochromatin.
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D DNA-FISH data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Increased nuclear Ikaros was sufficient for the repositioning of Igll1 to pericentromeric heterochromatin.
source: In contrast, most (78%) Igll1 alleles were associated with γ-satellite DNA after 4-OHT (Figure 6D), indicating that increased nuclear Ikaros cells was sufficient for the repositioning of Igll1 to pericentromeric heterochromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 3D DNA-FISH data.

claim: Ikaros-induced Igll1 repositioning was reduced to 55% of alleles by low doses (1 ng/ml) of TSA.
source: Ikaros-induced of Igll1 repositioning was reduced to 55% of alleles by low doses (1 ng/ml) of TSA (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D DNA-FISH data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: HDAC activity is required for full Igll1 silencing, even though it is dispensable for the early events in transcriptional repression.
source: Taken together, incomplete transcriptional silencing of Igll1, partial MNase protection of Igll1 promoter DNA and incomplete repositioning of Igll1 alleles to pericentromeric heterochromatin in the presence of HDAC inhibitors indicate that HDAC activity is required for full Igll1 silencing, even though it is dispensable for the early events in transcriptional repression (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments with HDAC inhibitors.

claim: The Ikaros-induced repositioning of Igll1 alleles was severely impaired (from 78% to 13%) by knockdown of Chd4.
source: We found that the Ikaros-induced repositioning of Igll1 alleles was severely impaired (from 78% to 13%) by knockdown of Chd4 (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D DNA-FISH data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Pericentromeric repositioning of Ikaros target loci requires NuRD-associated chromatin remodeling as well as HDAC activity.
source: Pericentromeric repositioning of Ikaros target loci therefore requires NuRD-associated chromatin remodeling as well as HDAC activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experiments showing both CHD4 and HDAC activity are required for repositioning.

claim: Chd4-depleted cells showed a steeper rise in Ikaros binding between 5 and 15 min than control cells.
source: Chd4-depleted cells showed a steeper rise in Ikaros binding between 5 and 15 min than control cells.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of ChIP kinetics data in control versus Chd4-depleted cells.

claim: The decrease in EBF1 binding seen in control cells was significantly blunted in the absence of CHD4.
source: Strikingly, the decrease in EBF1 binding seen in control cells was significantly blunted in the absence of CHD4.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of ChIP kinetics data in control versus Chd4-depleted cells shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Integration of MNase-seq with Ikaros ChIP-seq showed that nuclear translocation of Ikaros increases nucleosome occupancy at Ikaros ChIP-seq peaks genome-wide.
source: Consistent with a scenario where Ikaros not only displaces EBF1, but ultimately limits its own binding, integration of MNase-seq with Ikaros ChIP-seq showed that nuclear translocation of Ikaros increases nucleosome occupancy at Ikaros ChIP-seq peaks genome-wide (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by integrated analysis of MNase-seq and ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Nuclear translocation of Ikaros results in immediate binding to target gene promoters.
source: Here we take a high-resolution view at transcriptional repression based on the inducible nuclear translocation of Ikaros. Nuclear translocation of Ikaros results in immediate binding to target gene promoters, providing a clear path to target gene regulation.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the kinetic ChIP data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Kinetic ChIP shows half-maximal binding of Ikaros to the Igll1 target gene promoter within 5 min.
source: Kinetic ChIP shows half-maximal binding of Ikaros to the Igll1 target gene promoter within 5 min (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by kinetic ChIP data summarized in Figure 7D.

claim: Ikaros effected half-maximal removal of RNAP2, transcriptional silencing and promoter invasion by nucleosomes within 12 min of nuclear translocation.
source: Ikaros effected half-maximal removal of RNAP2, transcriptional silencing and promoter invasion by nucleosomes within 12 min of nuclear translocation (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by kinetic data summarized in Figure 7D.

claim: Ikaros recruited the NuRD-associated chromatin remodeller CHD4 to target promoters.
source: Ikaros recruited the NuRD-associated chromatin remodeller CHD4 to target promoters, and CHD4 was required for the invasion of the Igll1 and Myc promoters by nucleosomes, the exclusion of RNAP2, and the eviction of EBF1.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data showing increased CHD4 binding after Ikaros translocation.

claim: CHD4 was required for the invasion of the Igll1 and Myc promoters by nucleosomes, the exclusion of RNAP2, and the eviction of EBF1.
source: Ikaros recruited the NuRD-associated chromatin remodeller CHD4 to target promoters, and CHD4 was required for the invasion of the Igll1 and Myc promoters by nucleosomes, the exclusion of RNAP2, and the eviction of EBF1.
evidence: The claim is supported by CHD4 knockdown experiments showing impaired nucleosome invasion, RNAP2 eviction, and EBF1 displacement.

claim: Nuclear translocation of Ikaros reduced the accessibility of Ikaros binding sites genome-wide.
source: Nuclear translocation of Ikaros reduced the accessibility of Ikaros binding sites genome-wide.
evidence: The claim is supported by genome-wide MNase-seq analysis.

claim: Ikaros-induced chromatin remodeling limited the binding of the repressor itself.
source: Ultimately, Ikaros-induced chromatin remodeling limited the binding of the repressor itself, as evidenced by increased Ikaros binding after knockdown of Chd4.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that Ikaros binding increases in CHD4-depleted cells.

claim: Ikaros can reduce EBF1 binding to the Igll1 promoter only in the presence of CHD4.
source: Mechanistically, Ikaros can reduce EBF1 binding to the Igll1 promoter only in the presence of CHD4, and EBF1 is binding is sensitive to local chromatin structure (Treiber et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data showing that EBF1 eviction is impaired in CHD4-depleted cells, and citation to previous work.

claim: EBF1 binding is sensitive to local chromatin structure.
source: Mechanistically, Ikaros can reduce EBF1 binding to the Igll1 promoter only in the presence of CHD4, and EBF1 is binding is sensitive to local chromatin structure (Treiber et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Coincident with increased NuRD recruitment, the SWI/SNF-associated chromatin remodeler BRG1 was evicted from the Igll1 promoter.
source: Coincident with increased NuRD recruitment, the SWI/SNF-associated chromatin remodeler BRG1 was evicted from the Igll1 promoter.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data showing decreased BRG1 binding coincident with increased CHD4/MBD3 binding.

claim: BRG1 did not return to the remodeled Igll1 promoter even after the binding of CHD4 and MBD3 declined.
source: BRG1 did not return to the remodeled Igll1 promoter even after the binding of CHD4 and MBD3 declined, which may in part explain why promoter accessibility was not re-instated, suggesting that Ikaros-mediated NuRD recruitment and eviction of BRG1 may cooperate in the repression of Ikaros target genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP kinetics data and represents an inference about the mechanism.

claim: High-resolution view of Ikaros-mediated gene silencing indicates a temporal dissociation of enzymatic activities associated with NuRD where histone deacetylation occurred after chromatin remodelling and transcriptional repression.
source: Interestingly, our high-resolution view of Ikaros-mediated gene silencing indicates a temporal dissociation of enzymatic activities associated with NuRD where histone deacetylation occurred after chromatin remodelling and transcriptional repression (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by kinetic data summarized in Figure 7D showing different timescales for different events.

claim: CHD4, but not HDAC activity was required for reduced promoter accessibility, the loss of RNAP2, and transcriptional repression.
source: CHD4, but not HDAC activity was required for reduced promoter accessibility, the loss of RNAP2, and transcriptional repression.
evidence: The claim is supported by experiments with CHD4 knockdown and HDAC inhibitors.

claim: HDAC activity facilitated stable transcriptional silencing, nucleosome occupancy of target promoters, and locus repositioning to pericentromeric heterochromatin.
source: Although dispensable for the initiation of transcriptional repression, HDAC activity did facilitate stable transcriptional silencing, nucleosome occupancy of target promoters, and locus repositioning to pericentromeric heterochromatin.
evidence: The claim is supported by experiments showing effects of prolonged HDAC inhibition on gene silencing, nucleosome stability, and locus repositioning.

claim: The silencing mechanisms delineated are interdependent.
source: The silencing mechanisms delineated here are interdependent, as illustrated by the role of HDACs and the involvement of CHD4 in competition between Ikaros and EBF1 for access to the Igll1 promoter, RNAP2 occupancy and locus repositioning to repressive nuclear environments, a hallmark of heritable gene silencing (Brown et al., 1999; Su et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments showing connections between different silencing mechanisms, with citations to previous work.

claim: Both histone deacetylation and CHD4-mediated chromatin remodeling contribute to efficient repositioning of the Igll1 locus.
source: Our data link locus repositioning to chromatin state by demonstrating that both histone deacetylation and CHD4-mediated chromatin remodeling contribute to efficient repositioning of the Igll1 locus.
evidence: The claim is supported by experiments showing that both HDAC inhibition and CHD4 knockdown impair locus repositioning.

claim: At the Ikaros target genes Igll1 and Myc as well as genome-wide, RNAP2 recruitment, rather than RNAP2 elongation, was the primary mechanism by which Ikaros repressed RNAP2-dependent transcription.
source: At the Ikaros target genes Igll1 and Myc as well as genome-wide, RNAP2 recruitment, rather than RNAP2 elongation, was the primary mechanism by which Ikaros repressed RNAP2-dependent transcription.
evidence: The claim is supported by genome-wide analysis of RNAP2 occupancy patterns.

claim: Experimental depletion of RNAP2 and the resulting loss of RNAP2-mediated transcription did not interfere with Ikaros-induced promoter remodelling.
source: Experimental depletion of RNAP2 and the resulting loss of RNAP2-mediated transcription did not interfere with Ikaros-induced promoter remodelling.
evidence: The claim is supported by experiments with triptolide-mediated RNAP2 depletion.

claim: This is consistent with a direct role for Ikaros in target gene repression.
source: This is consistent with a direct role for Ikaros in target gene repression, and reminiscent of primary response gene induction in the absence of protein synthesis.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Ikaros can remodel promoters independently of RNAP2.

claim: Ikaros-mediated repression was unlike the induction of primary response genes with respect to the role of active chromatin remodeling.
source: With respect to the role of active chromatin remodeling, however, Ikaros-mediated repression was unlike the induction of primary response genes, and reminiscent of nuclear hormone receptor signaling where several enzymes cooperate to remodel chromatin within minutes of hormone addition (Ballaré et al., 2013; Grøntved et al., 2013; Nacht et al., 2016; Vicent et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a comparison to other systems with citations to previous work.

claim: The rapid repression of developmentally regulated genes utilizes complex and interdependent mechanisms.
source: The emerging picture is that the rapid repression of developmentally regulated genes utilizes complex and interdependent mechanisms, and that complexity does not come at the expense of speed in transcriptional state transitions.
evidence: This is a concluding statement summarizing the overall findings of the study.
